paper.title_en: Effective Field Theories for Precision Physics: Gradient Flow and Beta Decay
paper.abstract_en:
This thesis explores the application of effective field theory (EFT) techniques to two problems in precision particle and nuclear physics. The first part focuses on establishing a connection between non-perturbative lattice QCD calculations and continuum EFT descriptions using the gradient flow. The second part focuses on higher-order calculations for nuclear beta decays, which provide important tests of the Standard Model.


The gradient flow provides a theory in which composite operators are ultraviolet finite at non-zero flow time, making them suitable for lattice computations. The short-flow-time expansion (SFTE) relates these flowed operators to renormalized operators in the continuum, with matching coefficients that can be computed in perturbation theory. Regarding the gradient flow, this thesis presents several new results. First, the complete one-loop SFTE of the CP-odd three-gluon operator is computed, including its mixing with physical, nuisance, and evanescent operators. A notable feature is the emergence of power-divergent mixing into the QCD $\theta$-term, which must be subtracted non-perturbatively in lattice applications. Extending this result, the SFTE is performed for the full baryon- and lepton-number- conserving Low-Energy Effective Field Theory (LEFT) up to dimension six. This provides, for the first time, a perturbative connection between flowed operators accessible on the lattice and renormalized Wilson coefficients in the continuum, for arbitrary flavor structures. The structure of both logarithmic and power-divergent contributions is analyzed, offering guidance for their non-perturbative subtraction in future lattice calculations. In addition, we provide partial results for two-loop SFTE of the dipole operators, by providing the one-loop matching into evanescent operators and the $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$ physical matching.


Complementing these conceptual developments, a computational framework/pipeline is developed to automate EFT calculations, combining diagram generation, symbolic manipulation, and multi-loop integral reduction techniques.


In the second part of the thesis, we shift our attention to electromagnetic radiative corrections to nuclear beta decays. These corrections are essential to test the unitarity of the CKM matrix. The results contribute to improving the theoretical control required to match the increasing experimental accuracy.


Overall, this thesis advances the use of the gradient flow as a quantitative interface between lattice QCD and continuum EFTs, while also contributing to precision studies of weak processes. It provides new theoretical results and practical tools for high-order calculations in EFTs."><meta name="og:description" property="og:description" content="This thesis explores the application of effective field theory (EFT) techniques to two problems in precision particle and nuclear physics.
